plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: Six aldosterone-treated vs six vehicle-treated human kidney samples, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), unpaired, single batch. The plan runs the standard DESeq2 workflow grounded by the knowledge service: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) before any test; a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size); DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization baked into the model; an explicit reference level (control) with the Wald test for treated vs control; apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change; BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05 for the DE gene list. Downstream, the Wald statistic of every tested gene is used (never a thresholded subset) for two parallel analyses: (1) fgsea preranked enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, all present in the reference store for human; (2) decoupleR univariate linear model (ulm) transcription factor activity inference on the CollecTRI human regulon network (also present in the reference store), which is the grounded substitute for VIPER/ARACNe given the small n and no tissue-specific regulon. A final report step consolidates DE results, fit diagnostics, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and ranked TF activities, with full reproducibility metadata (versions, seed, collection releases).

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size QC
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
~condition design, explicit reference level = control, contrast treated vs control
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI regulons using the Wald statistic
Integrated DE + enrichment + TF activity report
